rounds.text: Pashupati Cotspin Ltd exhibits powerful fundamental momentum supported by robust profitability metrics and stellar multi-year growth figures, including a 3-year compounded profit growth of 39% [E16] and TTM profit growth of 17% [E17]. Operational efficiency is exceptional, underscored by a Mar 2026 cash conversion ratio of 3.70x and massive free cash flow of Rs 39 Cr, proving that reported earnings are entirely backed by hard cash [E27, E29]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is surging; foreign institutional holding has skyrocketed by 12.23 percentage points since March 2023 to reach 12.66% [E35], riding on a favorable sector tailwind score of +0.58 in textiles [E65, E66]. The company is actively deleveraging with borrowings falling to Rs 97 Cr [E32], while maintaining a comfortable current ratio of 2.02x [E31] and outperforming sector medians on ROCE at 12.42% [E10]. Conceded: [E38] A discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 17 per share against a market price of Rs 27.2 [E38].

Pashupati Cotspin is currently trading at a significant valuation premium that is not supported by its underlying financial performance, with a P/E ratio of 64.4x and a P/B ratio of 6.11x [E1, E2]. This valuation is starkly disconnected from sector benchmarks, where the company trades at a P/E of 68.21x against a sector average of 14.67x and an EV/EBITDA of 30.15x compared to a 9x benchmark [E6, E11]. The stock’s technical health is poor, as it sits near its 52-week low, remains below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and has suffered a 12-month price return of -11.8% [E5, E43, E45]. Furthermore, the company’s internal growth metrics show signs of fatigue, with trailing twelve-month sales growth at -2% and a median return on equity of only 7% over the last year [E15, E22]. A discounted cash flow analysis suggests the stock is significantly overvalued with a margin of safety of -64.6%, implying that the current price requires an unrealistic 24.9% earnings growth rate to justify [E38, E39, E40]. Conceded: the company maintains a comfortable current ratio of 2.02x, demonstrates strong cash conversion of 3.70x, and has seen a notable increase in foreign institutional ownership [E31, E27, E35].

Conceded: the P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples stand at 64.4x and 30.15x [E1, E11], and the DCF model points to negative margin of safety [E39]. However, the bear overlooks that profitability is actively outperforming expectations, evidenced by a profit growth of 17% in the trailing twelve months and 39% over three years [E16, E17], alongside recent margin expansion [E58]. Conceded: TTM sales growth is -2% [E15], but the broader picture reveals a healthy 3-year compounded sales growth of 16% [E14] backed by a strong sector tailwind score of +0.58 [E65]. Furthermore, technical proximity to 52-week lows [E5] does not negate stellar cash generation, as seen in the 3.70x cash conversion rate with Rs 39 Cr of free cash flow in March 2026 [E27, E29]. Finally, foreign institutions clearly recognize this underlying operational strength, aggressively raising their stake to 12.66% by September 2026 [E35].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at 17% alongside 39% over three years [E16, E17], and free cash flow reached Rs 39 Cr in March 2026 [E29]. Conceded: foreign institutions increased their holding to 12.66% by September 2026 [E35], yet overall institutional money flow is flagged as negative with a holding reduction of 0.27 percentage points [E37], and promoter stake has steadily declined by 7.05 percentage points since March 2023 [E34]. Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is 16% [E14] and the sector carries a tailwind score of +0.58 [E65], but trailing twelve-month sales growth has contracted by 2% [E15] and operating margins remain strictly inconsistent over recent periods [E25, E26]. Finally, the technical proximity to 52-week lows [E5] combined with a 0 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E44] demonstrates persistent market weakness rather than a mere temporary discount, leaving the share price trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43].
